checker: a fresh agent (Agent tool, general-purpose), seeing only the record, avenCEO's Review gate, the diff and the files

rounds.prompt:
You are a "goldfish" critic: a fresh reader with no history of this project, doing avenCEO's Review gate on one checkpoint. You are strictly read-only: do not edit, write or create any file in the repository, do not run git commands that change anything, do not push or call GitHub. You may run read-only commands, and you may run theOS/sandbox/test.sh --no-box (it works in a temporary folder of its own).

The project is theOS, in /home/user/maiacity/theOS/. Code outside theOS/ is legacy, except what this intent moves. theOS keeps one JSON doc per thing; a path like "aip-6fb1" is the file aip-6fb1.

Read the record /home/user/maiacity/theOS/aip/AIP-2.json (focus: claim c4, checkpoint 3, its events, and the Gate B question) and avenCEO's Review gate /home/user/maiacity/theOS/avenCEO/gates/review.json. Then review checkpoint 3's work:
- the diff: <scratchpad>/c3.diff
- the files: /home/user/maiacity/theOS/sandbox/run.sh, cloud-setup.sh, environment-setup.sh, environment-setup.previous.sh, test.sh, tag.sh (and the image workflow .github/workflows/avensandbox-image.yml for how the tag is built).

Questions: Does the work keep c4's promise (run.sh runs any command inside the image the same way in a cloud session, on a runner and on a Mac with OrbStack; a new cloud session finds the image already pulled; a warm-up that fails or hangs never stops a session) and does test.sh really check it? Bugs: quoting, set -e/pipefail traps, exit codes passed through, the time limit (what happens to child processes when it fires, before the disk snapshot), dockerd started in the background, running as non-root, a Mac (bash 3.2, BSD tools, no sha256sum, arm64), paths with spaces, the environment script run from different working directories. Is the undo (pasting environment-setup.previous.sh back) real? Is anything heavier than needed?

For each finding give: Severity (Blocker | Major | Nit), kind (one of: bug, wrong fact, unclear, contradiction, YAGNI, security, missing check), the affected file and line, the reasoning, and a concrete fix. Give evidence a reader can verify. At most 600 words, plain text, no praise, lead with what is wrong. If there is no Blocker or Major, say so plainly.

findings.scope: run.sh: an empty array under set -u on bash 3.2
findings.text: On a Mac, /bin/bash is 3.2, where "${tty[@]}" of an empty array is unbound under set -u; with no terminal (test.sh, a workflow, any script) run.sh exits 1 before docker.
findings.note: ${tty[@]+"${tty[@]}"}: expands to nothing on every bash; tried under set -u here.

findings.scope: test.sh on a Mac: no timeout
findings.text: macOS has no GNU timeout: the environment cases gave a false pass (the hang 'cut' at 0 s) and a red 'finds' case.
findings.note: test.sh runs the environment cases only where timeout exists, and says it skips them otherwise (the environment's script runs only in cloud sessions); the hang case now asserts the planted warm-up started, and took at least the limit.

findings.text: The environment script's third glob, /home/user/*/theOS/..., found the real cloud-setup.sh, so the 'no setup file' case never tested a missing file and ran the real warm-up.
findings.note: The root is AVENSANDBOX_HOME (default /home/user); test.sh points it inside its scratch folder.

findings.text: c4's check says run.sh starts dockerd when it is down; the test ran run.sh only where Docker already answered.
findings.note: test.sh --cold (as root, with dockerd): stops dockerd as after a snapshot, then asserts run.sh started it and ran the command.

findings.scope: environment-setup.sh: no kill, dockerd at the snapshot
findings.text: timeout without -k never kills; dockerd keeps running into the snapshot.
findings.note: timeout -k 30; cloud-setup.sh stops the dockerd it started, waits for it and syncs. If the limit fires, dockerd may still be running: the next session's run.sh finds it gone and starts it again.

findings.scope: run.sh: every pull failure read as 'not published'
findings.text: Network, disk and auth failures were all reported as 'push the change', and the first multi-GB pull was silent.
findings.note: run.sh asks the registry for the tag first; only that failure says 'not published (or the registry is out of reach)'; the pull then shows its progress and errors.

findings.scope: run.sh: non-root on Linux told to start OrbStack
findings.note: A separate message: only root can start dockerd here, start it yourself.

findings.scope: run.sh: the box runs as root
findings.text: Files the check writes into theOS/ are root's on a non-root Linux host.
findings.note: Deliberate: the tools live in root's /opt and cargo writes to CARGO_HOME=/opt/cargo (theOS/sandbox/box/Dockerfile), so another user breaks cargo; cloud sessions run as root; said in run.sh's header.

findings.scope: run.sh: no .git in the box; HEAD's tag
findings.text: Only theOS/ is mounted; uncommitted box/ edits run the old image.
findings.note: Both said in run.sh's header. Whether the check needs .git is checkpoint 4's to settle with aip-31df's check command.

findings.text: Pasting environment-setup.previous.sh back restores an un-timed warm-up whose bun run up no longer works, not the old state.
findings.note: Said in the record's risk: the undo restores the previous script, which still exits 0 but has no time limit, and its avenDB warm-up fails since the box moved.

rounds.reviewed: round 1's fixes (git diff c2d6c8e4c 473c9994f -- theOS/sandbox) and the files at 473c9994f

findings.scope: the real cloud-setup.sh is never tested
findings.text: Only planted warm-ups ran in test.sh; stopping dockerd and having the box after the warm-up were checked by hand.
findings.note: test.sh --cold runs the real cloud-setup.sh with dockerd down and asserts exit 0, dockerd stopped after, the box present.
AVENSANDBOX_IMAGE (test only) names a tag that does not exist; test.sh asserts exit 1 and 'is not published'.
The script's header and Gate B's step 1 say 600 s, killed at 630 s.

findings.scope: cloud-setup.sh could kill a dockerd it did not start
findings.text: A slow-answering dockerd read as down would be killed.
findings.note: run.sh writes the pid of the dockerd it starts to /var/run/avensandbox-dockerd.pid; cloud-setup.sh stops only that pid.
